_description: Task13 WEIGHTING field (unit probe), FINE transcription -- the 0.1mm grid used for BOTH the near-field solve and the final stitched volume, for the 5x5 LArPix v2a tile at the true 4.4mm pitch. The coarse sibling (example_gen_pixel_with_grid_task13_coarse.json) is the 0.22mm far-field grid. NOTHING IS SNAPPED HERE, the opposite of the coarse file: at 0.1mm every true design length is an exact whole number of cells -- pixelSize 3.5 -> 35 cells, pixelGap 0.9 -> 9, chamfer_r 0.7 -> 7 (via int(round()); 0.7/0.1 is 6.999999999999999 in binary float, so the rounding is load-bearing). PITCH: 3.5 + 0.9 = 4.4mm = 44 fine cells and 20 coarse cells. hybrid_iterate.py _cells() requires the transverse extent to be a WHOLE number of cells. PIXEL PLANE LOW EDGE 9.9 IS LOAD-BEARING: 9.9mm is 99 fine cells AND 45 coarse cells of 0.22mm, so the pad plane lands on a real node of BOTH grids; moving it breaks that co-location. NO GridPotential and NO CathodePotential, deliberately: the weighting potential is a dimensionless unit probe in [0,1], not volts -- collecting pixel = 1 and every other electrode including the cathode = 0 -- so the cathode formula in the drift configs does not apply here. DEPTH: driftZDepth 79.15 with pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition 9.9 tracks the drift pair's 69.25mm geometry; the weighting solve itself does not use a drift length, but the number is kept in step so the file handed to induce-pixel is not stale. The domain closes at ceil(79.15/0.22) = 360 coarse cells = 79.2mm = 792 fine cells exactly. SHIELD GRID OFF (GridHoleShape 'None', Phase 0/Step 8): inherited from the older with-grid task13 work and never intended for this WOGRID LArPix v2a geometry; the drift pair was cleared in Step 7 and these two must match it, since the drift field and the weighting probe have to model the same geometry. This was NOT inert while it was on: gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py:296 called draw_3Dstrips_sq, which writes into barr only, so the strips became a GROUNDED perforated electrode -- for a weighting field that is a Ramo non-collecting electrode held at W=0, shielding the pad. Verified on the coarse grid: the old grid plane (index 52 at 11.44mm) held 4400 cells and now holds none; the occupied planes are the pad block (44/45/46, 6400 cells each), the z=0 face and the cathode at 360. Transverse edges stay fix,fix,fix on the 22.0mm (5 x 4.4mm) domain. Effect on the far tail is large: coarse W on the pad-centre axis is 6.4x larger at z=25mm, 8.1x at 40mm and 10.5x at 60mm with the grid gone, because the grounded strips had been shielding it. NOTE the 'None' branch works by FALL-THROUGH -- there is no else on the circular/square test -- so any typo, 'squrae' for instance, also silently means no grid. PROBE: Npixels 5 at the 4.4mm pitch = 22.0mm transverse, i.e. 220 cells at this file's 0.1mm spacing (100 at the coarse 0.22mm), solved NON-periodic (edges fix,fix,fix) so phi_w decays to ~0 at the tile edges instead of wrapping; a weighting field cannot be solved on the single periodic pixel tile the drift field uses. GRID SIZE: 220 x 220 x 793 is about 38 M nodes, well down from the retired 9x9 / 0.0925mm transcription (360 x 360 x 1733, about 225 M). THIS file is also the one induce-pixel is handed for the pad-collection map, so its pad geometry must stay identical to the drift fine config's.
